To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
academic health centers need to develop new "innovation institutes" to prepare the next genration of physicians for the new payment models and to optimize their own value.

academic health centers are developing "innovation" institutes to help them prepare their trainees and faculty to deliver high value health care, and that innovation institutes are a promising model for teaching cost conscious care to medical educators and trainees.

innovation institutes can enhance value by: 1) providing leadership to overcome barriers to value based medicine, 2) educating faculty, house officers, and medical students, 3) engaging faculty, house officers and medical students to participate in quality improvement projects, and 4) facilitating scholarship to advance the science and practice of value based care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how academic health centers can best prepare for the transition to value based care.
how academic medical centers can be better prepared to meet the challenges and opportunities of the new healthcare environment.
the development and implementation of a new type of institute within an academic health center.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the innovation institute model has been a successful model in academic health centers.
academic health centers are well poised to lead the transformation to value based care.
academic health centers must transform themselves in the next decade to remain financially viable and relevant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development and implementation of an innovation institute is not a panacea for the financial and educational problems facing academic health centers in the United States, but it is a necessary first step in the right direction.

the innovation institutes are an important part of our strategy to improve patient care and reduce costs, and we believe that the innovation institute is an important model for other academic health centers to consider.
innovation and value institutes are critical to academic health centers in the next decade, but they are not the only solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
academic health centers must develop new organizational structures to enable them to be leaders in cost conscious care and to educate the next generation of leaders in value based care.
academic health centers must be able to demonstrate that they are leaders in value based care and cost conscious medicine.
innovation institutes have a critical role to play in the transformation of academic health centers to value based organizations.
